title: License Plate Reader Adds Device Snooping Feature
summary: Leonardo, a multinational aerospace and defense company, is marketing SignalTrace, an upgrade to its ALPR systems that captures Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and RFID identifiers from smartphones, wearables, and other devices near vehicles to create an 'electronic fingerprint' correlated to license plates. Security and privacy experts interviewed raise Fourth Amendment, cybersecurity, and mass-surveillance concerns about the technology.

key_quotes.quote: SignalTrace expands traditional ALPR capabilities by detecting and correlating electronic devices near vehicles of interest
the same feature that makes it useful for tracking a genuine suspect makes it equally capable of tracking everyone else on the road, none of whom consented to having their devices logged
The main problem with SignalTrace and other technologies similar to it is that they turn existing ALPR infrastructure into personal device trackers without anything that would require public review
the business model of ALPR companies is to outsource Fourth Amendment violations from the government to private companies, which sell the information back to the government
